resources.string:
Preview a solar eclipse

Sky Map can now show you how much of the Sun will be covered during an eclipse, as seen from where you are standing — including the total eclipse of 12 August 2026.

Two changes make this work together. The Moon\'s position now accounts for your location on Earth, not just the Earth\'s centre, correcting errors of up to a degree — about two Moon widths. And a new Show true-to-life sizes setting draws the Sun, Moon and planets at their real angular sizes instead of the enlarged markers used for visibility. Turn it on, then wind the time forward to watch an eclipse play out to scale.

More accurate Sun and Moon algorithm

Installed a more modern algorithm for Sun/Moon position to make eclipse timings even more accurate.

A tidier sky

  • Overlapping labels are now detected and nudged apart, so crowded regions stay readable.
  • Redrawn stars and constellations sidebar icons that were easy to confuse.

Sky Map v2 is coming — a complete rewrite. Join the beta to try it early (see above).
